Manual assembly monitoring

Catch skipped assembly steps at the bench

VisionInspect watches manual assembly and packing stations through a camera. It learns the correct work sequence from one recorded cycle and flags skipped steps, wrong order and cycle times that are too long or too short, live, while the part is still at the bench.

Request a demo contact@visioninspect.de
  • Learns from one correct cycle
  • Live check with a camera
  • Every cycle logged
  • Runs offline

Why steps get skipped

Manual assembly depends on people doing the same steps in the same order, cycle after cycle. Late in a shift, during a rush or with a new colleague, a step gets missed: a part not inserted, a label not applied, a manual not packed. Often nobody notices until the customer does.

VisionInspect checks every cycle on camera, so a missed step is caught at the bench, not in a customer complaint.

What it detects

  • Skipped steps

    A step in the sequence was not done.

  • Wrong order

    Steps were done in a different order than taught.

  • Repeated steps

    A step was done more than once.

  • Steps too short or too long

    A step took much less or much more time than expected.

  • Idle time

    Time in the cycle when nothing happened.

  • Cycle time against target

    Every cycle is logged with its time against the target, with CSV export.

How it works

  1. 01

    Record one correct cycle

    Upload a video of the work done right.

  2. 02

    Mark the steps

    Mark where each step starts and ends on the timeline.

  3. 03

    Click Learn

    VisionInspect learns the steps, then replays the teaching video by itself to check what it learned.

  4. 04

    Run it live

    Point a camera at the bench. Every cycle is checked and logged.

Checks the work instead of directing it

Worker guidance systems tell the operator what to do next. VisionInspect does something different: it watches what was actually done and flags deviations from the taught sequence. Apart from a camera pointed at the bench, the workstation stays as it is.

It can also follow an object, such as the box being packed, so its exact position on the bench doesn’t matter. It has been tested with 5-minute cycles; longer ones are possible.

Connects to your line

  • Modbus TCP

    Talk to your PLC directly, for example pulse a coil on FAIL.

  • MQTT

    Publish every result to your broker.

  • Webhooks

    Signed HTTP calls to your MES or other systems.

  • GPIO edge agent

    Switch lamps and relays, for example on a Raspberry Pi.

  • CSV / ZIP export

    Results, cycle logs and images for your records.

  • Any camera

    IP cameras via RTSP, USB cameras, a webcam, or a watched folder.

Questions

Does it record our workers?

It analyses the camera image to check the work steps. Everything stays on your own PC, you decide how long images and results are kept, and roles control who can see what. In Germany and many other countries, camera use at workstations should be agreed with your works council and data protection officer before you start.

How long can a cycle be?

It has been tested with 5-minute cycles; longer ones are possible.

Does the position of the part on the bench matter?

Not necessarily. VisionInspect can follow an object, such as the box being packed, so the steps are recognised wherever it is on the bench.

Can it also check the finished product?

Yes. The Industrial Inspection module in the same app checks finished parts against good ones and flags any deviation.

What happens when a step is skipped?

The cycle is flagged and logged. Through Modbus TCP, MQTT, webhooks or the GPIO edge agent you can tell your PLC or MES, or switch a signal lamp.
